correctness.rationale: The integral over the product box factors into normalized sinc(πkL)/(πkL) terms. For noninteger width, b1!=0, |b2/b1|=|cos(πL)| and πL|b1|=|sin(πL)| recover the unique positive width; b1 divided by signed sinc recovers exp(-2πic). An integer width has b1=0 and all other nonzero integer samples vanish. The recovered factors and common volume imply complete-spectrum equality iff identical integer-width axis set and noninteger widths/center residues, with arbitrary integer-side centers and product-preserving integer widths. The first-frequency-cube counterexample uses λ∈(1/2,1) with sinc(λ)=2/(3π), swapping λ and 3/2 and shifting centers by half. It agrees on the entire frequency-1 cube but not at 2e1. The strict sinc monotonicity for widths in (0,1) proves the special case. Independent floating-point reproduction checked 9360 samples, witness λ≈0.816725605 and nonzero second gap ≈0.218057. No finite test proves all d.
